prompt:
Write a single paragraph about a fictional weather station. The paragraph must satisfy ALL 16 constraints below simultaneously. Sentences are defined as maximal spans ending in `.`, `!`, or `?`. Words are whitespace-separated tokens.

1. The paragraph contains exactly 6 sentences.
2. The first alphabetic character of sentences 1 through 6, in order, spells `BREEZE`.
3. Sentence 1 contains exactly 9 words.
4. Sentence 2 contains exactly 10 words.
5. Sentence 3 contains exactly 11 words.
6. Sentence 4 contains exactly 12 words.
7. Exactly two sentences share the same first word.
8. The shared first word is `Every`.
9. The case-insensitive whole word `cloud` appears exactly 3 times.
10. The case-insensitive whole word `gauge` appears exactly 3 times.
11. The first occurrence of `cloud` appears earlier in the paragraph than the first occurrence of `gauge`.
12. Sentence 5 contains at least one whole-word occurrence of both `cloud` and `gauge`.
13. Exactly one sentence ends with an exclamation mark.
14. Sentence 6 ends with a question mark.
15. The whole paragraph contains between 74 and 82 words inclusive.
16. The only digit token in the whole paragraph is `7`, it appears in sentence 6, and the whole word `error` never appears.

Output ONLY the paragraph, nothing else.
difficulty_rationale: The acrostic, duplicated first-word rule, and sentence-local word counts constrain sentence openings together.
Three keyword-count rules interact with a positional rule that fixes which keyword must appear first.
The paragraph-level word band couples all local edits across six sentences.
Punctuation choices affect both sentence parsing and the exclamation/question constraints.
The unique digit token and forbidden-word rule punish casual revisions in the last sentence.
Exactly one pair of duplicate first words is allowed, so adding a natural repeated opener breaks a global constraint.
Because the checker uses maximal sentence spans ending in punctuation, stray punctuation changes the sentence inventory.
Even fluent prose can fail mechanically on only one count, so careful writers still slip on interacting constraints.
